issue_context.title: New SMA integration not using scan_interval: anymore.
issue_context.body:
### The problem

New SMA integration not using scan_interval: anymore.  
Instead, it polls the SMA device every 5 seconds, wich is too much for me at last.
(DEFAULT_SCAN_INTERVAL = 5)

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.5.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

SMA Solar

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sma/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?


2021-05-15 17:18:29 ERROR (SyncWorker_13) [homeassistant.util.json] Failed to serialize to JSON: /config/.storage/core.config_entries. Bad data at $.data.entries[27].data.scan_interval=0:01:00(<class 'datetime.timedelta'>
2021-05-15 17:18:29 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.storage] Error writing config for core.config_entries: Failed to serialize to JSON: /config/.storage/core.config_entries. Bad data at $.data.entries[27].data.scan_interval=0:01:00(<class 'datetime.timedelta'>



### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
[sma documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sma)
[sma source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/sma)
<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

Hey there @kellerza, @rklomp, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`sma`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L440) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Log entries are with:
scan_interval: 60
in configuration.yaml

Scan interval is a platform option,. this integration is no longer a platform.
So this is not a bug.

We are generally not adding options to change scan/polling intervals, as they generally cause more problems than they solve. Instead, we provide a sane default.

For a local device, 5 seconds is fast, but not generally problematic.

> wich is too much for me at last.

Could you explain the problem with it? Because if it causes issues, it would be a bug.

I have created https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/50679 to implement an option flow to change scan interval. I don't think setting it to anything other than the default 5 seconds will cause any problems.

Anyhow, @frenck it's up to you if you want to merge this or not.
We rather not have it, instead we should have sane defaults. So, unless we are solving a big issue that cannot be solved with a sane default, that PR should not be merged.

5 second default scan time is a bit insane when polling a webserver that runs in slow hardware IOT device.
I don't want to see my solar-controller crash due to hammering the webservice every 5 seconds. (it uses SSL, wich is quit CPU intensive) In the existing code, there is the option to use a non-default timer, and it worked till the integration...

5 seconds isn't insane, it is pretty standard for local polling integrations in many platforms.


Could you provide a stack trace of the crash?

Even for a slow iot device 5 seconds is a long time for something as simple as a web response. I polled my sunnyboy at 5 seconds for years.

Storing 5s data is excessive, but easy to average it with a filter and only record that average. This might even be documented somewhere on the pysma integration/one of the historical issues on the repo

no, no stack trace, the SMA conrollers are 'closed'. no logging. 
My device  is the 'instap-model', maybe it has a slower CPU.
5 seconds just doesn't add any extra value: totals are counted in the device itself, and it puts unnecessary stress on the device. the polling works through a webservice, that is not meant to be polled every five seconds. 
Why not just let the end-user decide? (we had the possibility, it was asked by many users, not only me!)

@kellerza so... you have to add a filter for something that could be just simple as increasing the default poll-time, or just make it user-configurable. This is home-assistant right? not an apple product? We can change polling of numerous stuff....
And a 'simple web response' isn't that simple when using SSL. Maybe i have to revert to plain http wich is not ok.

Are you actually experiencing crashes? Or afraid of crashes?

What kind of device do you have?
My device has no issues with the 5 sec interval and it is working fine.

i've had an unresponsive web-server once when polling with the default timer, but i can't prove that the poll-rate is the culprit. Just powered off my sunnyboy 3000.  Changed polling rate to 60. Not seen a  unresponsive webserver again. But can't prove anything. (maybe half-open tcp connections due to bad wifi in the garage *COULD* be the culprit)
Hey, i'm not going to make a crusade over this and i greatly (as an prof. ITer myself for 20 year) respect the work you're putting into it... just strange that making a previous configurable (logic to me) option work *again* leads to this kind of polemic.

As a workaround could manually update the `/config/.storage/core.config_entries` file.
Find the entry for SMA and set 
```json
                "options": {
                    "scan_interval": 60
                },
```
Keep in mind that this is not a supported way of configuring and it is not guaranteed it keeps working. But it might still work for now. Also.. Make a backup of the file first to easily roll back in case of issues.

edited the file:
```
                    "sensors": [],
                    "custom": {},
                    "options": {
                        "scan_interval": 60
                    },
                    "device_info": {

```
unfortunately doesn't change the behaviour... Thanks for the try @rklomp .

*EDIT* WRONG edit from my side... will try again

Those files SHOULD NOT be edited by hand, it will cause you problems eventually.

@rklomp As one of the maintainers of the integration, you are shooting yourself in the foot doing that. Additionally, that should not work, if so, it means we have dead code that should be removed.
config in that file is re-written anyways.
@wimpie007 Yes, it is not for "manual" consumption, it is a result of/managed by code.

@wimpie007 
We could change the default scan interval to 10 seconds for all users. Would you be happy with that?

All sensors are not equal. 

Any total you can measure at 1min even 5min, it is probably not that important, but there are other (and probably more interesting) instantaneous values, where even 5 seconds feels like a long time today, and that it why I use the filter @wimpie007. Once we up the default we take all flexibility away from the user.

Maybe we could only add total values to the request every 30seconds/1min, but this is obviously more complicated since we have to mark these in pysma and use it in the integration, but at least you're not taking choice away from the end user. Up to now I didn't do this, since the filter is a good working solution in 99.9% of the cases. It's also the first time I heard about a request crashing a Sunnyboy. If you open the web portal (which supports only a single session) your favorite browsers hammers it continuously for 5+ seconds loading the interface, all graphs, etc

> Maybe we could only add total values to the request every 30seconds/1min, but this is obviously more complicated since we have to mark these in pysma and use it in the integration, but at least you're not taking choice away from the end user. Up to now I didn't do this, since the filter is a good working solution in 99.9% of the cases. It's also the first time I heard about a request crashing a Sunnyboy. If you open the web portal (which supports only a single session) your favorite browsers hammers it continuously for 5+ seconds loading the interface, all graphs, etc

I don's see any added value of that. It only makes things more complicated, but does not reduce the amount of requests. It will still do a request every 5 seconds, but with a bit less data.

To be honest I dont see why the 5 second interval should cause any issues. Even when you visit the webinterface of the device using your browser it is using a 5 second refresh interval to query **all** values. And even some extra values in a second request. Thus 2 request per 5 seconds instead of 1 per 5 seconds that Home Assistant is now doing.

but you don't leave the webinterface 24/7 open...
Anyway...  just wanted to let you know that a functionality is missing since the integration, and that there are people who don't like the 5s interval and then having to use filters to store the values.
If you guys don't want to fix/add it again, thats your decision.  I'm just a user.

@wimpie007 you originally posted this as an issue that breaks something. Could you please be so kind to provide logs? That allow us to dig in an see what can be improved.

Thanks!
as already written, the SMA device became unresponsive to any web-requests. power off/on fixed it.  No logs from the SMA device...
But it should show something on the HA side?

Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue has now been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.
